page: Amazon Web Services r5b.24xlarge is a memory-optimized instance powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture with an Intel Xeon 8259CL processor operating at 3.1 GHz. The configuration provides 96 virtual CPUs across 48 physical cores with hyperthreading enabled. It includes 768.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, translating to 8.0 GB of RAM per core. This instance does not include local storage or GPU hardware, and it delivers a baseline network bandwidth of 25 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks indicate strong multi-core capabilities and memory throughput, contrasted by weaker single-core performance. The stress-ng multi-core CPU test and Passmark CPU score both rank in the top 25%, reflecting high parallel processing capacity. Memory bandwidth is also highly efficient, with read-only small block cached speeds reaching 4502.42 GB/sec and large block uncached write speeds at 97.63 GB/sec. However, single-core performance is relatively weak, as shown by the stress-ng single-core CPU and single-threaded gzip compression benchmarks, which fall into the bottom 25%.

Given its high memory density and strong multi-core throughput, the r5b.24xlarge is highly suited for memory-intensive workloads such as large-scale in-memory databases, caching layers, and enterprise applications. This is supported by its strong Redis SET operations benchmark of 74.14 million operations per second and static web serving throughput of 43.34 GB/sec. Qualitatively, the instance offers high resource density for memory-bound tasks, though the lack of local storage requires external network-attached storage, and the weaker single-core performance makes it less optimal for single-threaded compute tasks.
